question.problem:
Consider the equation in the variable $v,$ given by

$$
2(q-7)v+5=1
$$

where $q$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $q?$

$q=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

First, let's write our equation in the form $av=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(q-7)v+5 & =1 \\ 2(q-7)v+5-5 & =1-5 \\ {{2(q-7)}_{⏟}}_{a}v & ={{-4}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

$$
2(q-7)=0.
$$

Solving this for $q,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(q-7) & =0 \\ \frac{2(q-7)}{2} & =\frac{0}{2} \\ q-7 & =0 \\ q & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
